title: The revision is ordered, starting with Bihar
what_changed: The Election Commission ordered a Special Intensive Revision "in the entire country", starting with Bihar, with the schedule for the rest of the country to follow. Only electors whose enumeration forms came back would be on the draft roll. The 2003 Bihar roll, from the state's last intensive revision, was treated as evidence of eligibility, including a presumption of citizenship. Anyone not on it had to give documents from an indicative list of 11, and the younger the elector, the more were needed. Those born before 1 July 1987 gave their own. Those born up to 2 December 2004 gave their own and one parent's, and those born later gave their own and both parents'. A new declaration had to go with every Form 6 for a new voter, and with Form 8 for anyone moving into Bihar. No name could be deleted from the draft without an inquiry. Appeals lay to the District Magistrate and then the Chief Electoral Officer, the Commission's officer in charge of the roll in each state.
documents: ECI order of 24.06.2025 and letter of 27.10.2025, as published by CEO Kerala | CEO Bihar, press notes on the SIR, 2025

title: Bihar's schedule
what_changed: Enumeration, the round of forms, was set for 25 June to 26 July 2025. The draft roll was due on 1 August, claims and objections were open from 1 August to 1 September, and the final roll was due on 30 September 2025. Forms received before 25 July would go into the draft.
documents: ECI order of 24.06.2025 and letter of 27.10.2025, as published by CEO Kerala

title: The 2003 roll goes online
what_changed: The 2003 Bihar roll, with 4.96 crore electors, was put online. Anyone on it needed no documents. Anyone not on it could use a parent's entry in it in place of documents for that parent.
documents: CEO Bihar, press notes on the SIR, 2025

title: The Supreme Court hears the challenge
what_changed: The Court issued notice on the petitions against the 24 June order. It observed that the Commission should also consider Aadhaar, the voter identity card and the ration card, but gave no direction to accept them. This account of the hearing comes from the Court's judgment of 27 May 2026.
documents: Supreme Court, judgment of 27.05.2026, 2026 INSC 564

title: Bihar's draft roll
what_changed: The draft roll was published, and claims and objections were open until 1 September. No name was to be deleted from the draft without a hearing and a written order.
documents: ECI press release of 01.08.2025 (PIB)

title: The names left off must be published
what_changed: The Court recorded the Commission's agreement to publish the roughly 65 lakh names left off the draft with the reason for each. The lists were to go up district by district, searchable by EPIC number (the number on the voter identity card), online and on panchayat and block notice boards. The public notice was to say that a claim could be made with a copy of Aadhaar.
documents: Supreme Court order of 14.08.2025

title: Political parties brought in
what_changed: Twelve political parties were made parties to the case. They were told to have their booth agents help voters file forms with any of the 11 documents or with Aadhaar. This account of the order comes from the 2026 judgment.
documents: Supreme Court, judgment of 27.05.2026, 2026 INSC 564

title: Claims after the deadline
what_changed: The Commission told the Court that claims, objections and corrections could still be made after 1 September and would be considered up to the last date of nominations. The Court directed the chairman of the Bihar State Legal Services Authority to have the district legal services authorities send para-legal volunteers to help voters and parties file them online. This account of the order also comes from the 2026 judgment.
documents: Supreme Court, judgment of 27.05.2026, 2026 INSC 564

title: Aadhaar becomes the 12th document
what_changed: The Court directed that Aadhaar be accepted as the 12th document, as proof of identity. The Court said it is no proof of citizenship, and the authorities remained free to verify each card.
documents: Supreme Court order of 08.09.2025

title: The Commission follows the order
what_changed: The Commission told the Chief Electoral Officer of Bihar that Aadhaar is the 12th document, as proof of identity, and that it is no proof of citizenship.
documents: ECI letter of 09.09.2025 to CEO Bihar

title: Bihar's final roll
what_changed: The final roll was published with about 7.42 crore electors. Appeals lay to the District Magistrate and then the Chief Electoral Officer.
documents: ECI press release of 30.09.2025 (PIB)

title: Twelve more states and union territories
what_changed: The revision was extended to Andaman and Nicobar, Chhattisgarh, Goa, Gujarat, Kerala, Lakshadweep, Madhya Pradesh, Puducherry, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal, on the June order with changes. No documents were to be collected while forms were filled in. The form asked instead for the elector's own entry, or a relative's, in the state's last intensive revision, and after the draft notices would go only to those who could not be linked to it. For every form not returned, the booth-level officer (BLO), the official who looks after the roll for one polling booth, was to record a probable reason (absent, shifted, dead or duplicate). The declaration with Form 6 was changed, and BLOs were to carry at least 30 blank copies of Form 6 with it.
documents: ECI order of 24.06.2025 and letter of 27.10.2025, as published by CEO Kerala

title: Which old roll counts
what_changed: Each state's forms are linked to the roll of its last intensive revision, and the Commission fixed which year that was. Linking an elector to that old roll is called mapping. West Bengal, Kerala, Rajasthan, Gujarat and Goa go back to 2002. Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Bihar go back to 2003. Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Tripura, Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh go back to 2005, and Arunachal Pradesh to 2006. Tamil Nadu has two, 2002 for 197 seats and 2005 for 37.
documents: ECI order of 24.06.2025 and letter of 27.10.2025, as published by CEO Kerala

title: The first Phase II schedule
what_changed: Enumeration was set for 4 November to 4 December 2025 and the draft for 9 December. Claims ran to 8 January 2026, notices to 31 January, and the final roll was due on 7 February 2026.
documents: ECI order of 24.06.2025 and letter of 27.10.2025, as published by CEO Kerala

title: Assam gets a different revision
what_changed: Assam was given a "Special Revision" in place of an intensive one. Booth officers were to check house to house from 22 November to 20 December 2025, with a register already filled in for them. The draft was due on 27 December, claims ran to 22 January 2026, and the final roll was due on 10 February 2026. The pages read give no reason for the difference.
documents: ECI letter of 17.11.2025 to CEO Assam (instructions listing, eci.gov.in)

title: Anta gets its own dates
what_changed: Rajasthan's Anta seat could not follow the 27 October schedule because a bye-election was under way, so it was given its own. Enumeration started on 8 December 2025, the draft was due on 12 January 2026, claims ran to 11 February and the final roll was due on 12 March 2026.
documents: ECI letter of 27.11.2025 for 193-Anta, CEO Rajasthan

title: Every Phase II date moves a week
what_changed: All twelve states and union territories got one more week. Enumeration now ran to 11 December, the draft was due on 16 December, claims ran to 15 January 2026, notices to 7 February, and the final roll was due on 14 February 2026.
documents: ECI order of 30.11.2025, as published by CEO Goa

title: Lists before the draft
what_changed: Before the draft, Chief Electoral Officers were to give party booth agents the booth-wise lists of those absent, shifted, dead or duplicated. After it, they were to put the lists online, searchable by EPIC number.
documents: ECI press release of 10.12.2025 (PIB)

title: Seven move again
what_changed: At the request of their Chief Electoral Officers the dates moved again. Tamil Nadu and Gujarat got drafts on 19 December, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Andaman and Nicobar on 23 December, and Uttar Pradesh on 31 December. Kerala had already been moved to a draft on 23 December. The same release also lists Gujarat among the states keeping the 16 December draft, and does not name Puducherry.
documents: ECI press release of 11.12.2025 (PIB)

title: The "logical discrepancy" list
what_changed: The Court said names in the "logical discrepancy" category, flagged because something in their link to the old roll did not match, may be displayed at panchayat, block and ward offices. Documents could be filed through an authorised representative such as a booth agent, the Commission was to allow ten more days from the display, and the Madhyamik admit card may be accepted.
documents: Supreme Court order of 19.01.2026, W.P.(C) 1089/2025

title: More officers to help
what_changed: The Court had 8,505 state officers report to the district and registration officers to assist them, with the final decision left to the registration officers. Scrutiny was given at least a week beyond 14 February.
documents: Supreme Court order of 09.02.2026

title: Judges decide the claims
what_changed: Using its powers under Article 142, and with the parties' consent, the Court gave the deciding of claims and objections about inclusion to judicial officers of West Bengal, acting "for and on behalf of this Court". This account of the order comes from the Court's orders of 2 and 13 April 2026.
documents: Supreme Court order of 02.04.2026 | Supreme Court order of 13.04.2026

title: Judges from Jharkhand and Odisha, and no appeal to officials
what_changed: A further order set out the work given to the judicial officers and said their orders could not be appealed before any executive or administrative officer. Judicial officers from Odisha and Jharkhand joined those of West Bengal, and by 10 March there were 200 of them beside more than 500 from West Bengal. This account of the order comes from the Court's order of 10 March 2026.
documents: Supreme Court order of 10.03.2026

title: West Bengal's final roll, with 60 lakh held back
what_changed: The final roll was published with 60,06,675 names marked "under adjudication". They were to be added by a supplementary list if the judicial officers approved them.
documents: CEO West Bengal, press note CEO/PN-05/2026

title: Appeals go to tribunals
what_changed: No executive officer could hear an appeal against an order of the judicial officers. Appeals were to go to tribunals of former Chief Justices and judges, which the Commission would notify in consultation with the Chief Justice of the Calcutta High Court.
documents: Supreme Court order of 10.03.2026

title: Nineteen tribunals
what_changed: Nineteen appellate tribunals were at work. Appeals decided by 21 and 27 April were to take effect through a supplementary roll before polling, and a pending appeal gave no right to vote.
documents: Supreme Court order of 13.04.2026

title: The rest of the country
what_changed: The revision was ordered in 16 states and 3 union territories, covering the whole country except Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, whose dates would be announced later. Eight separate schedules were set. After the draft, notices would go to those who could not be linked to the last intensive revision (the no-mapping list) and to those whose link showed a discrepancy. Lists of those sent notices were to be published.
documents: ECI press note ECI/PN/086/2026 of 14.05.2026 (PIB) | Copy of the ECI order of 14.05.2026 (district site)

title: The Supreme Court upholds the revision
what_changed: The Court disposed of the petitions. It held that the revision has its legal basis in section 21(3) of the Representation of the People Act read with Article 324, that it was proportionate, and that its document list, with Aadhaar added, was not arbitrary. The Commission may enquire into citizenship only for electoral purposes and must refer doubtful cases to the competent authority of the Central Government. People domiciled in Bihar whose names were wrongly deleted as absent, dead, shifted or duplicate may seek judicial review.
documents: Supreme Court, judgment of 27.05.2026, 2026 INSC 564

title: Mizoram avoids Sundays
what_changed: At its Chief Electoral Officer's request, Mizoram's draft moved from Sunday 5 July to 4 July 2026, and its final roll from Sunday 6 September to 7 September.
documents: CEO Mizoram press note of 04.07.2026 | CEO Mizoram press releases

title: Karnataka three weeks later
what_changed: Karnataka's draft came out on 24 August 2026 instead of 5 August. Enumeration ran to 17 August, claims to 23 September, and the final roll was set for 27 October instead of 7 October. It was published on 27 October.

title: Maharashtra four weeks later
what_changed: Maharashtra's draft came out on 31 August 2026 instead of 5 August. Claims were to run to 30 September, and the final roll was then due on 4 November instead of 7 October. On 26 September the Commission extended claims to 12 October and moved the final roll to 16 November.
documents: CEO Maharashtra press note of 31.08.2026 | PTI in ThePrint, 26 September 2026

title: Documents at the door, and a drive for those left off
what_changed: For people sent notices as unmapped or for logical discrepancies, BLOs would collect documents at home and upload them for the registration officer, so these people need not come to the office. A hearing would be held only in exceptional cases, as the registration officer decides, preferably online, and a family member authorised by the elector could attend. The Commission said the declaration attached to Form 6 for the revision had been upheld by the Supreme Court, and that outside the revision the forms in the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 apply. Claims were extended in Delhi to 30 October and in Maharashtra to 12 October 2026. Where the revision was complete, in 20 states and union territories, anyone left out during it or after, and any young or first-time voter, could ask the registration officer to be added under continuous updation, and the Chief Electoral Officers, district officers and registration officers were to launch a special drive at once to enrol them.
documents: ECI press note ECI/PN/120/2026 of 26.09.2026 | ECI press release of 26.09.2026 (PIB)

title: Andhra Pradesh and Meghalaya extended
what_changed: Andhra Pradesh's notices were to run to 10 October and its final roll was then due on 16 October 2026. On 14 October the Commission extended the notices to 22 October and moved the final roll to 30 October. Meghalaya's final roll moves to 26 October 2026, and it was published that day.
documents: ECI press release of 30.09.2026 (PIB) | Chief Electoral Officer, Andhra Pradesh, post of 14 October 2026 | Deccan Chronicle, 15 October 2026

title: The drive after the revision, in writing
what_changed: The Commission wrote to every Chief Electoral Officer setting out a special drive to enrol electors left off and young or first-time voters. Booth officers are to compare the current roll with the roll from before the revision, list everyone who was on the first and is missing from the second, visit them at home and help those found eligible fill in Form 6. The Commission asked them to cover at least 20 to 25 electors a week, so the work ends in about a month. The lists go to the booth agents of the recognised parties and then to the registration officer, who decides each case under the 1950 Act and the 1960 Rules. Booth camps are to be held, and special camps for people in night shelters, labour colonies and the homeless. The letter says anyone not on the roll, or whose name was deleted, can apply to be enrolled at any time.
documents: ECI letter No. 23/2025/ERS(Vol-II) of 01.10.2026 to all Chief Electoral Officers

title: A drive to find the names left off
what_changed: When it published Uttarakhand's final roll, the state's Chief Electoral Officer set out the Commission's directions for what follows. Booth officers are to compare the roll from before the revision with the current one and list the electors who were on the first and are missing from the second. They are to visit them at home and help those still eligible fill in Form 6. The lists are to be shared with the booth agents of the recognised parties, and booth and special camps held, including for people in night shelters, labour colonies and the homeless.
documents: CEO Uttarakhand, press note PN 63/2026 of 03.10.2026

title: A summary revision where the revision is over
what_changed: The Commission ordered a special summary revision of the roll, under section 21 of the 1950 Act, with 1 January 2027 as the qualifying date, in 17 states and union territories. They are the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Goa, Gujarat, Kerala, Lakshadweep, Madhya Pradesh, Manipur, Puducherry, Punjab, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and West Bengal. Polling stations are to be rearranged by 2 November, the draft rolls published on 12 November, claims and objections taken until 11 December and decided by 28 December, and the final rolls published on 4 January 2027. Claims for 1 April, 1 July and 1 October 2027 can be made in advance. No claim may be refused, and no name deleted, because a person cannot give an Aadhaar number. Recognised parties are to get each polling station's roll at the draft and at the final, on paper and as a readable PDF without photographs, with the lists of additions, deletions and changes, and a printed list of claims and objections every week. The registration officer must check deletions in person where they pass 2 per cent of a polling station's roll or one person has objected in more than five cases, and the limits on Form 7 set by the Commission's letter of 9 October 2026 apply. The letter says the dates for the states and union territories where the revision is going on or has just ended will be announced later. It names Andhra Pradesh, Arunachal Pradesh, Chandigarh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, Delhi, Haryana, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Odisha, Sikkim, Telangana and Tripura. The dates for Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, where the revision has not begun, are to follow with their weather in view.
documents: ECI letter No. 23/2026-ERS of 15.10.2026 to the Chief Electoral Officers of 17 States/UTs, as published by CEO Kerala

title: West Bengal's summary revision put back
what_changed: The Commission accepted a proposal of West Bengal's Chief Electoral Officer to change the dates of the special summary revision in West Bengal, in a letter the Chief Electoral Officer's office gave the press on 28 October 2026, PTI reported. The qualifying date stays 1 January 2027. Polling stations are to be rearranged by 13 November, the draft roll published on 23 November, claims and objections taken from 23 November to 22 December and decided by 8 January 2027, and the final roll published on 16 January 2027. The Commission's letter of 15 October had set the draft roll for 12 November and the final roll for 4 January 2027 in all 17 states and union territories of the summary revision. The Hindu of 31 October gave the draft roll in West Bengal as 11 November and the final roll as 16 January. The Chief Electoral Officer's website lists the revised schedule dated 28 October.
documents: PTI in ThePrint, 28.10.2026 | CEO West Bengal, revised schedule of the SSR dated 28.10.2026 (as listed on the CEO's home page)

title: Final rolls moved in five states and Delhi
what_changed: The Commission revised the schedule in five states and Delhi on 29 October 2026, after requests from their Chief Electoral Officers. In Maharashtra, claims and objections run to 13 November and notices and claims are to be decided by 25 November. In Delhi, claims and objections run to 25 November, notices and claims are to be decided by 15 December and the final roll is due on 22 December. Notices are to be decided by 20 November in Haryana and Andhra Pradesh, by 25 November in Nagaland and by 26 November in Telangana. The final roll in the five states is due on 30 November. The final rolls had been due on 30 October in Andhra Pradesh, 6 November in Haryana, 9 November in Telangana, 16 November in Maharashtra, 22 November in Nagaland and 4 December in Delhi. The revision came the day after the Supreme Court heard the petition on Delhi's revision on 28 October. At that hearing the Chief Justice told the Commission not to go by any cut-off date while no election was due in Delhi, and the press reported that the bench passed no order.

title: Tripura's revision put back a second time

Preparation, training and printing now run from 15 to 24 December. An official quoted by IANS gives the qualifying date as 1 January 2027, and Hindustan Times says it had been 1 October 2026.

title: Gujarat's summary revision put back
what_changed: Divya Bhaskar reported on 29 October 2026, citing a press note of the office of Gujarat's Chief Electoral Officer issued that day, that the Election Commission had revised the schedule of the special summary revision for the state under section 21 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, giving the present situation as the reason. title: Form 6 for electors who were on the roll before
what_changed: The Commission wrote to the Chief Electoral Officers of every state and union territory about electors whose names are not in the draft roll of the revision. Its letter says some of them were hesitant to file Form 6, whose declaration says the name is being included in the roll for the first time, because they believed that, having been enrolled before, they would be making a false declaration punishable under section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950. The letter says the declaration in Form 6 has been in force since 1 August 2022, that an elector whose name is not in the draft roll may file Form 6 to seek inclusion in the final roll, and that such an elector has to seek inclusion afresh during the revision or afterwards, whether or not the elector was enrolled before. It says a Form 6 filed in these circumstances "is not, by itself, false merely because the elector was previously enrolled". It directs that no registration officer is to start action under section 31 against an elector only because the elector was on an earlier roll and has filed Form 6 during the revision or afterwards, provided the elector is not already enrolled in any other parliamentary or assembly constituency and the declaration is otherwise in accordance with law. The letter cites the Delhi High Court's order of 14 October 2026 in W.P.(C) No. 14955 of 2026, which closed a petition by two electors and left them free to file Form 6. It asks the Chief Electoral Officers to give the clarification wide publicity, in local languages as well. The letter does not mention Form 8 or the enumeration form.

title: A summary revision in six more states and union territories
what_changed: The Commission ordered a special summary revision of the roll, under section 21 of the 1950 Act, with 1 January 2027 as the qualifying date, in 6 states and union territories where the revision has ended. They are Arunachal Pradesh, Chandigarh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, Mizoram, Odisha and Sikkim. Polling stations are to be rearranged by 20 November, the draft rolls published on 30 November, claims and objections taken until 30 December and decided by 16 January 2027, and the final rolls published on 21 January 2027. Claims for 1 April, 1 July and 1 October 2027 can be made in advance. The Commission's letter to the six Chief Electoral Officers refers to its instructions of 29 September for a special drive to enrol eligible electors who were left out, young electors and those voting for the first time, The Indian Express reported. The dates for Andhra Pradesh, Haryana, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Delhi, Tripura and Telangana, where the revision is going on or has just ended, are to be announced later, and those for Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, where it has not begun, with their weather in view. documents: The Indian Express, 05.11.2026 | NewsDrum, 05.11.2026

title: One more chance for electors marked absent, shifted, dead or duplicate
what_changed: The Commission wrote on 6 November 2026 to the Chief Electoral Officers of Delhi, Maharashtra, Haryana, Andhra Pradesh, Jharkhand, Telangana and Nagaland that electors who were issued an enumeration form but were left off the draft roll because they were marked absent, shifted, dead or duplicate are to be given one more opportunity to be included in the final roll. The booth-wise lists of these electors, whose forms were not received back, are to be put up again with the probable reason each was left off, on the notice boards of the polling stations concerned and at panchayat bhawans, urban local body offices and the offices of block development officers, and uploaded on each Chief Electoral Officer's website in a readable PDF. Partially filled enumeration forms are to be generated afresh on the registration officers' dashboard in ECINET, and the District Election Officers and registration officers are to make every possible effort to reach these electors through the booth level officers and to see the forms delivered, in person or by WhatsApp, email or SMS where contact details are available. The booth level officers are to try to reach each elector with the parties' booth level agents, by house visits, through neighbours, family and resident welfare associations, and by telephone. An elector can also download and fill the form on the Commission's website or the ECINET app with the EPIC number held before the name was left off. An elector who has not moved submits the form with a statement of why it was not submitted earlier, in person or through a family member, to the registration officer, the assistant registration officer or the booth level officer, or online on ECINET with an e-sign. An elector who has moved within the state need not file Form 8, and submits the form with a statement of the new address and Assembly constituency and proof of address to the registration officer or the assistant registration officer of the new constituency. For a homeless elector with no address document, the booth level officer's field verification report serves as proof of residence. The registration officers are to decide the forms under rule 21(1) of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, verifying eligibility and ordinary residence, with field verification where needed, and the forms accepted are to be kept apart for inclusion in the final roll, with the electors' earlier EPIC numbers. An elector who has already filed Form 6 during the revision need not submit the enumeration form, and that application is to be decided under the Commission's letter of 3 November. The Chief Electoral Officers and District Election Officers are to publicise the measures, by public announcement with loudhailers as well where homeless people live, and to send the Commission a report of the action taken. The letter, No. 23/INST/2025-ERS, is signed by the Commission's Secretary, Pawan Diwan, and sets no last date for the forms. The Times of India reported on 7 November that nearly 47.6 lakh electors were left off Delhi's draft, and that an official said the forms had not yet begun to be generated. The Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh called the letter a belated admission that wrongful deletion and exclusion had taken place, PTI reported. The final rolls in the six states are due on 30 November and Delhi's on 22 December.

They are Karnataka and Meghalaya. The draft rolls are to be published on 1 December, claims and objections taken until 31 December and decided by 14 January 2027, and the final rolls published on 20 January 2027. Claims for 1 April, 1 July and 1 October 2027 can be made in advance. Hindustan Times reported the order as a notification of 16 November 2026 and quoted it for Karnataka. The Hindu reported that it covers Meghalaya as well, and The New Indian Express described it as an order to the states and union territories where the intensive revision has ended, which on 16 November were Karnataka and Meghalaya. The New Indian Express reported that polling stations are to be rearranged on 23 November. The registration officer must check deletions in person where they pass 2 per cent of a polling station's roll or one person has objected in more than five cases, and in each case of deletion must pass a reasoned order after giving the person a hearing and upload it on ECINET. Hindustan Times reported that the order refers to the Commission's instructions of 9 October 2026 limiting the number of Form 7 applications one elector can file. No claim may be refused, and no name deleted, because a person cannot give an Aadhaar number. The Times of India reported that officials deployed for the revision cannot be transferred from 1 December 2026 to 20 January 2027 without the Commission's permission. An official of the office of Karnataka's Chief Electoral Officer told The New Indian Express that booth level officers will not visit homes with forms, as they did in the intensive revision, and that electors being added or deleted will be checked against the list of electors marked absent, shifted, dead, duplicate and others that was prepared for the intensive revision. The paper also reported that cases will not be heard as they were in the intensive revision. The notification itself could not be fetched from the Commission's website.

title: Dates for the forms of electors marked absent, shifted, dead or duplicate, and final rolls on 22 December
what_changed: The Commission wrote on 17 November 2026 to the Chief Electoral Officers of Maharashtra, Delhi, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Nagaland, Haryana and Jharkhand that the enumeration forms of electors left off the draft roll as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate are to be generated and printed by 18 November, handed out and collected from 18 to 30 November, and decided by 10 December, Hindustan Times reported. The paper reported that the letter also moved the dates of the revision in the six states other than Delhi and left Delhi's schedule as it was. Notices and claims and objections are to be decided in the six states by 15 December and the final rolls published on 22 December, the dates set for Delhi on 29 October. Their final rolls had been due on 30 November. Telangana Today and Deccan Chronicle listed Delhi among the states whose schedule was revised, and gave the same two dates. Telangana Today reported that the Commission's Under Secretary, Sandeep Kumar, fixed 15 December for Telangana, where notices had been due to be decided by 26 November, and that the Commission sent the revised schedule to the state's Chief Electoral Officer in a letter. Hindustan Times quoted the letter as saying that the booth-wise lists of these electors are to be displayed afresh on the notice boards of the polling stations, and that their enumeration and the modified schedule are to be given wide publicity through all available media. The paper reported that the arrangement of 6 November had begun on the ground only in Delhi and Jharkhand. It found on 17 November that it had yet to begin in at least four states, Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Haryana, and that its progress in Nagaland was unclear. Haryana's Additional Chief Electoral Officer, Raj Kumar, told the paper that the office was awaiting the printing of the forms, which might take five or six more days, and that the work would start after that. A spokesperson of Telangana's Chief Electoral Officer said no new forms were being generated and electors were still using Form 6. In Jharkhand, Additional Chief Electoral Officer Subodh Kumar said the forms were available and a special drive would be held on 18 November. Telangana's Chief Electoral Officer, C. Sudharshan Reddy, set out the same dates for Telangana in a press note of 18 November. The forms of these electors are to be handed out and collected from 18 to 30 November and decided by 10 December, notices and claims and objections decided by 15 December, and the final roll published on 22 December, Telangana Today (PTI) and The Times of India reported. The Times of India reported that the Commission's letter of 6 November had laid down the procedure and its letter of 17 November set the dates.

title: Delhi's drive for electors marked absent, shifted, dead or duplicate
what_changed: Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer announced in a press note of 17 November a special drive under the Commission's letter of 6 November, for electors who were issued an enumeration form but were left off the draft roll because they were marked absent, shifted, dead or duplicate. The note says the booth-wise lists of these electors are displayed on the notice boards of the polling stations, at the offices of the registration officers and the District Election Officers and with the booth level officers, and on the websites of the Chief Electoral Officer and the District Election Officers. An elector can fill the form on the Commission's website or the ECINET app with the EPIC number held before the name was left off, or get it from the booth level officer in person or by WhatsApp, SMS or email. An elector at the same address submits it with Annexure B, giving the reason it was not submitted earlier, to the registration officer, the assistant registration officer or the booth level officer, in person or through a family member, or online on ECINET with an e-sign. An elector who has moved within Delhi submits it with Annexure C, giving the new address and Assembly constituency, and proof of address, to the registration officer or the assistant registration officer of the new constituency, and need not file Form 8. Such an elector can ask the booth level officer of the new booth for help through the Book a call with BLO facility on the Commission's website or the ECINET app. The note says the same EPIC number the elector held before the revision is re-assigned once the form is accepted, and that an elector who has already filed Form 6 need not submit the form, the application being processed under the Commission's instruction of 3 November. It says new applicants who turned 18 on or before 1 October 2026 may apply on Form 6. PTI reported in The Telegraph that officials said on 17 November that the forms had begun to be handed out in Delhi, and that the forms are to be collected until 30 November and decided by 10 December. PTI reported in ThePrint on 18 November that booth level officers in Delhi said they had yet to receive the forms or detailed instructions, and that officials of the Chief Electoral Officer's office said the forms were being printed and would be sent to the registration officers on 19 November, with distribution to begin after that. The Chief Electoral Officer's press note of 31 August gave the names left off Delhi's draft as 47,56,722 of the 1,45,10,299 on the earlier roll, 43,32,775 of them marked permanently shifted, absent or other, 2,82,412 dead and 1,41,535 enrolled at more than one place.

title: Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer transferred
what_changed: The Ministry of Home Affairs ordered on 18 November that Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer, Ashok Kumar, be transferred to Jammu and Kashmir with immediate effect and until further orders, The Indian Express reported on 19 November. Kumar, a 2006-batch IAS officer of the AGMUT cadre, had been Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer since February, and the order moves him with two other senior officers from Delhi to Jammu and Kashmir. The paper says the transfer comes while the office is verifying electors and running its drive for electors left off the draft roll of 31 August as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate, which the Chief Electoral Officer's press note of 17 November announced. It does not say who will take over or give a reason for the transfer, and it carries no comment from the Ministry, the Commission or the officer.

title: Andhra Pradesh's drive for electors marked absent, shifted, dead or duplicate
what_changed: Andhra Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer, Vivek Yadav, announced in a press release of 19 November, posted in English and Telugu on the office's account on X, another opportunity for electors marked absent, shifted, dead or duplicate whose enumeration forms were not received back and who were left off the draft roll published on 31 July 2026. The release says the Commission took the decision after reports in the press and electronic media and protests by political parties that a large number of electors had been deleted during the revision although they were living at their addresses. It says the lists of these electors are available at the polling stations, at panchayat and municipal offices, at the offices of the registration officers and the assistant registration officers, and on the Chief Electoral Officer's website. The enumeration forms are to be generated again and delivered by the booth level officers in person, or by WhatsApp, email or SMS where contact details are available, and an elector can also download and fill the form on the Commission's website or the ECINET application with the existing EPIC number. An elector who has not moved submits the form with a statement in Annexure B to the registration officer, the assistant registration officer or the booth level officer, in person, through a family member or online with an e-sign on ECINET. An elector who has moved within Andhra Pradesh need not file Form 8, and submits the form with a statement in Annexure C and proof of address to the registration officer or the assistant registration officer of the new Assembly constituency. The forms are to be handed out and collected until 30 November. The release says that once a form is verified and approved, the elector keeps the original EPIC number and the name is included in the final roll to be published on 22 December, that an elector who has already filed Form 6 during the revision need not apply again, and that electors can use the Book a Call with BLO facility on the Commission's website or application. PTI reported the release the same day. The Chief Electoral Officer had announced the same opportunity in a press note of 7 November, Memo No. 610/Elecs.B/A1/2026-139, when the final roll was due on 30 November. That note says the registration officers are to decide the forms under rule 21(1) of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, and that for a homeless elector with no address document the booth level officer's field verification report serves as proof of residence.

title: West Bengal's summary revision postponed
what_changed: The office of West Bengal's Chief Electoral Officer postponed the special summary revision in West Bengal in press note No. 77/CEO/PN/2026 of 20 November 2026, signed by the Additional Chief Electoral Officer, Arindam Niyogi, and posted on the office's account on X. The note says the programme of the revision scheduled from 23 November 2026 onwards is postponed due to some unavoidable circumstances, and that a modified schedule will be intimated subsequently. It gives no other reason and no new date. Under the dates the Commission accepted on 28 October, the draft roll was to be published on 23 November, claims and objections taken until 22 December and decided by 8 January 2027, and the final roll published on 16 January 2027. Press note No. 75/CEO/PN/2026 of 13 November had set eight special campaign days, the Saturdays and Sundays from 28 November to 20 December, and the note of 20 November does not mention them. The Times of India reported that a senior official of the Commission cited administrative issues and said the decision was limited to West Bengal, and that another official said the rearrangement of polling stations, due by 13 November, had not been done. It reported that the Chief Electoral Officer's office also told the District Election Officers that the draft roll would not be published on the scheduled date. Hindustan Times quoted an official of the Commission, who asked not to be named, as saying that the decision was taken by the state Chief Electoral Officer's office alone, and that a revised schedule will have to be approved by the Commission before it is notified. The Indian Express reported that sources familiar with the process cited delays in the work of the tribunals hearing appeals against exclusion from the roll as one possible reason, and that a source in the Commission said the revised rolls had yet to be made available to the state Chief Electoral Officer's office.

title: Maharashtra's drive for electors marked absent, shifted, dead or duplicate
what_changed: Maharashtra's Chief Electoral Officer announced in a press note in Marathi of 20 November 2026, posted on the office's account on X, that the Commission has made enumeration forms available again for electors left off the draft roll published on 31 August 2026 because they were not living at their address or did not return the form. The note says the lists of these electors, marked absent, shifted, dead, duplicate or other, are on the websites of the Chief Electoral Officer and the District Election Officers and will also be made available at the polling stations. The forms are to be handed out and collected until 30 November. The booth level officers are to contact the electors marked absent or shifted who are not on the draft roll and fill in their forms, and an elector can also fill the form online on ECINET with an e-sign. An elector left off the draft roll is to contact the booth level officer of the part of the roll, and can do so through the Book a call with BLO facility on the Commission's website or the ECINET app. An elector marked absent, shifted, dead or duplicate who has not moved submits the signed form with Annexure B, and one who has moved submits it with Annexure C in the constituency the elector has moved to. The form can be submitted online, in person or through a family member to the registration officer, the assistant registration officer or the booth level officer, or in the same way to the booth level officer at special camps to be held on 28 and 29 November 2026.
